title: Clearing `@export` variable from an instantiated scene does not update parent scene save state
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in 4.5.1-stable
- Reproducible in 4.6.1-stable
- Reproducible in 4.7-dev2

### System information

NixOS, Godot 4.6.1-stable

### Issue description

When clearing an `@export` variable from an instantiated child scene, the editor (rightfully) recognizes that the scene state has changed.
Saving the scene does not update the scene on disk, however.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c7bdad81-b798-46a9-8ab2-32113aa5c6cc

Setting the export to an external Node, then deleting that external node, will properly update the `@export` variable to not be assigned on disk.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a scene with a script at the root that has an `@export` variable
2. Set it's `@export` variables to one of it's children.
3. Save the scene.
4. Instantiate this scene as a child scene in a parent scene.
5. git add or git commit the state.
6. Clear the `@export` variable
7. Save the parent scene.
8. You'll notice no change in the scene save state.
9. Reboot Godot
10. The `@export` variable will be reset to the value set in the child scene.

Optional to confirm that you _can_ clear `@export` nodes; do this after running above steps.
1. Create a node in the parent scene of the same type of the `@export` variable
2. Assign it as the `@export` variable.
3. Save the scene.
4. Delete the assigned node.
5. Save the scene.
6. Notice how the save state now correctly indicates that the `@export` variable is cleared.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[scene-save-bug-demo.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/25852603/scene-save-bug-demo.zip)

Above project is the same as in the demo gif, for 4.6.1-stable
